property_summary: After locking in a guess at block n, settling must still revert at block n+1 because the recorded target block is n+1; the mutant records n, letting settle succeed at n+1 for some inputs.

For any caller and any guess hash, lockInGuess must record the target block as the immediately-next block (block.number+1), so that settling two blocks later (block.number+2) always succeeds; the mutant records block.number+2 and therefore reverts on settle at that block for some inputs.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,bytes32): settle at target+1 blocks must succeed

property_summary: In the reference C, after a user successfully settles, their guess slot is cleared so any subsequent settle() reverts; the mutant never clears the slot, so a second settle() succeeds (or pays out again), breaking the one-shot-settlement rule.

In the reference C, settle() clears the caller's guess slot, so after any settle() the caller can always lockInGuess a new hash (one-shot settlement frees the slot); the mutant never clears the slot, so lockInGuess afterwards reverts.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(bytes32,bytes32,address): after settle, a new guess must be lockable

property_summary: For any caller and any guess, a completed settle never changes the contract's 1-ether balance (a correct guess pays out only if 2 ether is available, which it never is, and a wrong guess pays nothing); the mutant pays 1 ether on a correct guess, draining the balance.

For any admissible fuzzed (actor, rollAhead) the winning settle in the reference pays out the entire 2-ether balance (address(c).balance == 0 afterward), whereas the mutant pays only 1 ether, leaving address(c).balance == 1 for the same inputs.

For every admissible actor, a winning settle on C must revert because the payout (2 ether) can never be covered by the 1-ether-funded contract, whereas the mutant pays out 1 ether and succeeds, draining the balance.

When a player wins (blockhash is 0 for blocks >256 old) and the pool holds 2 ether from two locks, settle must pay the full 2 ether and drain the contract to balance 0; the mutant pays only 1 ether, leaving 1 ether behind.

For any player who locks a guess and settles more than 256 blocks later (so the target blockhash is 0 and the guess wins), C's 2-ether pool (1 ether from the constructor plus the player's 1 ether) is fully paid out, leaving address(c).balance == 0; the mutant pays only 1 ether, leaving 1 ether behind.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,uint256): winning settle must drain the full 2-ether pool

property_summary: For any actor who locks a winning guess and later settles, the contract must pay out exactly 2 ether, so address(c).balance decreases by 2 ether on every winning settle; the mutant omits the transfer, leaving the balance unchanged.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,uint256): winning settle must transfer 2 ether out of the contract
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,uint256): winning settle must transfer 2 ether out of the contract

property_summary: For any actor who locks the guess keccak256(bytes32(0)) and settles more than 256 blocks later (so the target blockhash is provably 0 and the guess provably wins), the contract must pay out 2 ether, i.e. its balance drops by exactly 2 ether; the mutant omits the transfer so the balance is unchanged.

For any actor, after locking a guess and settling once the winning block's hash is provably 0 (gap >= 257 blocks), the correct contract must pay out the 2-ether prize, leaving address(c).balance == 0; the mutant omits the transfer, so the balance stays at 2 ether.
A call to lockInGuess with exactly 1 ether must succeed (not revert), which fails in the mutant requiring 2 ether.
A fresh caller with no prior guess can successfully lock in a guess (lockInGuess does not revert); the mutant inverts this and reverts.

property_summary: lockInGuess accepts exactly 1 ether and rejects every other value, for all callers and all amounts.
The very first lockInGuess from an address that has never guessed must succeed (not revert), since the guess slot starts at zero.
A first lockInGuess call from a fresh account with exactly 1 ether always succeeds (the contract accepts exactly 1 ether, not 2).
A caller with no prior guess can lock in exactly one guess: the first lockInGuess succeeds and an immediate second one from the same caller reverts.
From a fresh account, the first lockInGuess succeeds and an immediate second lockInGuess from the same account reverts, because a guess can be locked only when no guess is pending.
